Education / K-12 schools

Calmer admissions, safer school days and parents who hear what matters

K-12 schools talk to families every day about admissions, attendance, buses, homework, fees and results. We connect the school ERP to one official WhatsApp number parents opt in to, the parent app and staff dashboards, so parents get timely, private updates, teachers lose repetitive admin and the principal can see what was sent, read and escalated.

The challenge

What makes k-12 schools different.

01

Admission season brings a flood of enquiries and campus tour requests that the front office handles by phone, with little follow-up once the call ends.

02

Absence and bus updates depend on a teacher or the transport in-charge finding time to call, so a child who did not arrive may not be noticed quickly.

03

Class WhatsApp groups mix circulars, homework and chatter, expose parents' numbers to each other and leave no record of who read a safety notice.

04

Daily substitutions are planned on paper before assembly, and the same willing teachers absorb much of the extra cover.

05

Fee follow-up by phone and noticeboard is slow and awkward, and can embarrass children when dues are raised in class.

Where automation helps

Practical uses for k-12 schools.

01

Enquiry-to-tour admissions desk

Enquiries from ads, the website and walk-ins logged with their source, answered from the approved prospectus, and moved to a campus tour with reminders and counselor follow-up.

02

Same-day absence alerts

Students marked absent without approved leave trigger a private message to the parent by mid-morning, with reply buttons. Parents who did not know get a call from the class teacher or coordinator.

03

Bus boarding, drop and delay updates

Boarding and drop events from bus RFID readers or the attendant's app notify the parent, and route delays are announced only after the transport in-charge approves the message.

04

One channel for circulars, homework and PTMs

Teacher-approved homework digests and circulars per child, translations checked by a fluent teacher, acknowledgment tracking for consent slips, and PTM slot booking from teachers' calendars.

05

Substitution plans before the first bell

A fair substitution plan proposed from the timetable and leave records, approved by the vice-principal and sent to substitutes with the absent teacher's lesson notes.

06

Private fee reminders and secure report cards

Courteous reminders and instant receipts sent only to the fee payer, and report cards released behind secure links once the principal locks results.

Discover and enquireStandard3–5 weeks

Admissions enquiries, counselor follow-up and campus tours

Enquiries from ads, the website, fairs, walk-ins and WhatsApp land in one CRM with their source, get an approved acknowledgment and a named counselor, and move to a campus tour or open-day slot with reminders and post-visit follow-up.

K-12 schools · Colleges & universities

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

In admission season, enquiries arrive faster than the front office can return calls. Leads sit in counselors' personal phones and spreadsheets, families who asked for a tour never get a slot, and the institution cannot tell which campaign or fair produced confirmed admissions.

Trigger

A parent or applicant submits a Meta or Google lead form or the website form, scans a fair or walk-in QR code, or messages the admissions WhatsApp number.

How it runs

  • Create or update one CRM record per family, de-duplicated by phone number, with source, campaign, grade or program, campus, and the consent and notice version shown on the form.
  • Send families who opted in an approved WhatsApp acknowledgment with the prospectus link and the counselor's name, assigned by grade or program, campus and language; send the rest an email or DLT-registered SMS.
  • Answer common questions on fees, transport, dates and eligibility only from the approved prospectus and fee schedule; route anything else to the counselor with a short summary.
  • Offer campus tour and open-day slots from the admissions calendar, share directions and a visitor pass for the gate, and remind the family the day before with a one-tap reschedule.
  • After the visit, prompt the counselor to record the outcome and send the registration or application link the family asked for.
  • Escalate enquiries with no counselor contact within the agreed time to the admissions head, and report enquiries, tours and admissions by source each morning.

Human checkpoint

Counselors make every follow-up call and record outcomes, and the admissions head approves templates, answer content and assignment rules. The workflow never screens or ranks children or parents, and seats under RTE Section 12(1)(c) follow the state's own portal and process.

Collects the enquirer's name, phone, grade or program and source. For K-12 the enquirer is the parent, and child details wait for the application. Consent and notice version are stored with the record, campaigns target parents and adult applicants only, and enquiries that do not lead to admission are deleted after the retention period the institution sets.

How we measure it

  • Enquiry-to-tour conversion
  • Tour-to-application conversion
  • Enquiries with no follow-up after the agreed time
  • Media cost per confirmed admission by source

Attend and learnStandard3–5 weeks

Absence, late arrival and school bus alerts to parents

Students marked absent without approved leave trigger a private message to the parent by a set time, with reply buttons, and bus boarding, drop and delay updates come from RFID or attendant app events. Unresolved cases reach a staff member who calls the family.

K-12 schools · Coaching & test-prep institutes

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Calling every absent student's family takes a teacher's free period, so calls are late or skipped. Parents of bus students cannot tell whether their child boarded, and the transport office spends the morning answering the same calls.

Trigger

The attendance cutoff passes with a student marked absent and no approved leave, or a bus RFID reader or the attendant's app records a boarding, drop or delay.

How it runs

  • At the cutoff the institution sets, read attendance from the ERP or biometric system and list students absent without approved leave.
  • Send the parent an approved WhatsApp utility template with buttons for known reason, arriving late or did not know, or a DLT-registered SMS if they have not opted in, and log the reply.
  • When the parent did not know or has not replied in the agreed time, alert the class teacher or coordinator on a dashboard so a staff member phones the family.
  • On RFID or attendant app events, notify the parent of boarding and drop, and send route delay notices only after the transport in-charge approves them.
  • If a child expected at a drop point is not marked off, alert the transport in-charge and the bus attendant at once to resolve by phone.
  • Show daily absences, late arrivals and unresolved cases, and give counselors a weekly list of repeated absences to follow up personally.

Human checkpoint

A named staff member phones every family that did not know about an absence, and the transport in-charge handles every missed drop or unusual delay by phone. Absence patterns are reviewed by the counselor or coordinator and never trigger automatic action.

Tools

Systems it connects

  • Biometric or RFID attendance devices
  • GPS and RFID bus tracking
  • Transport route master

Data & consent

Uses student name, class, attendance status, route and boarding events, sent only to registered parent numbers, and location stays inside the transport system the school controls. Schools rely on the DPDP educational and transport-safety exemptions only where their legal owner confirms they apply, otherwise on recorded parental consent. Boarding logs are kept for the one year the DPDP Rules require, then deleted.

What we deliver

  • Absence alert flow with parent replies
  • Bus boarding, drop and delay notifications
  • Unresolved case dashboard for staff
  • Approved template set

How we measure it

  • Parents notified of unexplained absence by the agreed time
  • Unresolved absences followed up by phone the same day
  • Boarding and drop notifications delivered
  • Calls to the transport office per day

Attend and learnStandard3–4 weeks

Circulars, homework digests and PTM booking for parents

Teachers post homework and circulars once in the ERP. Parents receive one daily digest per child in their chosen language, acknowledge consent slips with a tap, and book parent-teacher meeting slots from teachers' calendars.

K-12 schools

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Class WhatsApp groups mix homework, circulars and chatter, expose parents' numbers to each other and leave no record of who read a trip consent slip or a safety notice. PTM scheduling takes days of back-and-forth, and translated circulars depend on whoever has time.

Trigger

A teacher or coordinator publishes homework or a circular in the ERP, or the school opens a PTM window for a class.

How it runs

  • Collect the day's homework and approved circulars per class and assemble one digest per child at a time the school sets.
  • Draft translations into the languages parents chose, for a teacher fluent in that language to check before release.
  • Send the digest on WhatsApp to opted-in parents and through the parent app or email to the rest, with links to attachments instead of files in chat.
  • Track acknowledgments for circulars that need them, such as trip consent, and remind only the parents who have not responded.
  • For PTMs, offer slots from each teacher's availability, confirm with the room or video link, and send a reminder on the day.
  • Report delivery, acknowledgments and PTM attendance by class to the coordinator.

Human checkpoint

Class teachers approve their digests, a fluent teacher approves each translation, and the principal approves every school-wide circular and any message about safety, discipline or an incident. Parents' replies raising a concern go to the class teacher, not to an automated answer.

Attend and learnStandard3–4 weeks

Teacher absence and substitution planner

Leave recorded before a cutoff produces a proposed substitution plan from the timetable, matching free teachers by subject and sharing extra periods fairly. The vice-principal approves it, and substitutes get their periods and lesson notes before the first bell.

K-12 schools · Coaching & test-prep institutes

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Substitutions are worked out on paper before assembly by the one person who knows the timetable. The same willing teachers absorb much of the extra cover, lesson notes rarely reach the substitute, and in coaching an absent faculty member can leave a batch waiting with no class.

Trigger

A teacher records leave in the ERP or HR system, or submits a leave request through the staff form, before the daily cutoff.

How it runs

  • Read approved and pending leave for the day and list the periods or batch lectures that need cover.
  • Find teachers free in each period, preferring the same subject and class, and balance cover using each teacher's load for the week and term.
  • Show the proposed plan to the vice-principal or academic coordinator, with conflicts and unfilled periods highlighted.
  • On approval, notify each substitute with class, room and the absent teacher's lesson plan link, and update the display timetable.
  • In coaching, offer the coordinator a reschedule option for lectures that cannot be covered, and notify the batch once it is approved.
  • Report substitution load by teacher and term so leadership can see whether cover is shared fairly.

Human checkpoint

The vice-principal or academic coordinator approves every plan and can override any assignment. Leave approval stays with the principal or HR under the staff leave policy; the planner never approves or rejects leave.

Assess and reportStandard3–4 weeks

Report cards and results released securely to families

Once the principal or examination controller locks results, each report card or grade card is generated and the parent or adult student is notified with a secure, expiring link. PTM booking or revaluation options follow in the same notice.

K-12 schools · Colleges & universities

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Report cards are printed, signed and handed out on one crowded day, or forwarded as PDFs in groups where they can reach the wrong family. Corrections after release are messy, and colleges field calls about grade cards, revaluation windows and supplementary exams.

Trigger

The principal or examination controller marks results as final in the ERP or examination system for a class, program or semester.

How it runs

  • Generate each student's report or grade card from the locked results using the approved template and the remarks teachers entered.
  • Check for missing marks, unapproved remarks or records the exam office has flagged, and hold those until the exam office clears them.
  • Notify the parent or adult student with an approved template and a secure link that opens after a one-time code, never the document in chat.
  • Include the PTM booking link for schools, or revaluation and supplementary exam windows and fees for colleges.
  • Log every open, resend on request, and point families to DigiLocker where the board or university issues documents through it.

Human checkpoint

The principal or examination controller locks results and approves release, and teachers own their remarks. Revaluation, grace marks and any hold on a result are decided only by the examination office under the institution's rules, never by the workflow.

Pay, renew and stay connectedStarter2–3 weeks

Respectful fee reminders, payment links and receipts

Fee payers receive courteous reminders before and after due dates with a UPI payment link, receipts arrive instantly, and installment, concession or refund requests go to the accounts office. Reminders never reach children, class groups or noticeboards.

K-12 schools · Colleges & universities · Coaching & test-prep institutes

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Accounts staff chase dues by phone, reminders sometimes reach the wrong parent or a class group, and children can be embarrassed when dues are raised in class. Installment and refund requests get lost between the front office and accounts, and receipts are issued by hand.

Trigger

A fee installment approaches or passes its due date in the ERP fee ledger, a payment succeeds or fails at the gateway, or a fee payer asks about fees.

How it runs

  • Read due dates, amounts and concessions from the ERP fee ledger and send an approved reminder to the registered fee payer a set number of days before the due date.
  • Include a payment link for UPI, cards and net banking, post successful payments to the ERP ledger through its API or import, and send an instant receipt, or a GST invoice where the fee is taxable.
  • After the due date, send no more than the agreed number of courteous reminders, each with an option to request an installment plan or speak to accounts.
  • Route installment, concession, scholarship and refund requests to the accounts officer with the student's ledger summary and the applicable refund policy.
  • Give accounts a daily view of dues, promises to pay and failed payments, with no list shared with teachers or classes.

Human checkpoint

The accounts officer decides installment plans, concessions and refunds, and the principal or registrar approves reminder wording and frequency. Any step that affects a student's classes, exams or results is a management decision under the institution's policy and the law, never automated.
